llm.summary: This skill is a local CloudArc benchmark helper whose file access, Python execution, and artifact generation match its stated testing purpose.

dimensions.detail: The helper runs tests and benchmarks locally and can intentionally consume substantial temporary disk/time for manual 1/5/10 GiB runs, but this is disclosed and gated by --yes.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains normal skill files, references, registry metadata, and a local Python helper; no remote payload retrieval, dependency installation, or tool replacement behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to CloudArc benchmark, SLO, telemetry, CI, and documentation work, with explicit cautions not to use credentials, cloud services, proprietary packages, or unrelated user changes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No background service, scheduled task, memory poisoning, credential use, or cross-session persistence was found; persistence is limited to expected benchmark JSON/Markdown outputs and possible user-directed repository edits.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's purpose is to inspect a CloudArc repository, run bounded-memory benchmark/test workflows, validate telemetry, and update related benchmark contracts; its Python helper and instructions align with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only for CloudArc benchmark and telemetry work. Expect it to run local Python tests and benchmark commands and to write benchmark reports; use the manual mode only when you intentionally want a large run that may take hours and use tens of GiB of temporary disk.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill does require repository reads and Python execution for benchmark validation, but the artifact declares tools: [python] and repeatedly narrows behavior to local CloudArc files and no credentials/cloud activation, so this does not create a Review-level concern.
[AST4] expected: The subprocess call is used by the bundled helper to run explicit unittest and benchmark commands with argument lists and shell=False by default; inputs are user-supplied CLI options for a local benchmark helper, so the finding is purpose-aligned rather than evidence of command injection or malicious execution.
